title: Immune Defenders: Body at War
description: Command your immune system to stop waves of pathogens from infecting the body! Deploy T-Cells, Macrophages, Antibodies, and Fever Responses to neutralize viruses, bacteria, parasites, and superbugs. Learn how your body's real defense system works through strategic tower defense gameplay.
learning_objectives: Understand how the immune system identifies and fights pathogens
Learn the roles of T-Cells, Macrophages, and Antibodies in immune defense
Discover how vaccines prepare the body to fight infections
Recognize different types of pathogens: viruses, bacteria, parasites, and superbugs
Understand the concept of fever as an immune response mechanism
how_to_play: Waves of pathogens (viruses, bacteria, parasites, superbugs) invade the body along blood vessels.
Place immune defense towers along the path: T-Cells, Macrophages, Antibodies, and Fever Responses.
Each tower costs Antibodies to deploy — earn more by destroying pathogens.
Macrophages deal splash damage to groups of pathogens. Fever Responses slow enemies down.
If too many pathogens reach the end, the body gets sick — game over!
Survive all 8 waves to keep the body healthy and win!

storybook_pages.title: Invasion Alert!
storybook_pages.text: Pathogens have breached the body's outer defenses! Viruses, bacteria, and worse are flooding through the bloodstream toward vital organs. As commander of the immune system, you must rally your cellular defenders to stop the invasion before it's too late.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: inside the human body with blood vessels as pathways, colorful immune cells standing guard, menacing virus and bacteria characters approaching, dramatic lighting with red and blue tones, cartoon educational style

storybook_pages.title: Know Your Defenders
storybook_pages.text: T-Cells are your frontline soldiers — fast and reliable. Macrophages engulf groups of invaders at once. Antibodies are precision snipers that target pathogens from a distance. And when things get dire, the Fever Response heats things up, slowing all nearby enemies.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: four immune cell characters illustrated as heroes: a T-Cell warrior with a sword, a large Macrophage eating germs, an Antibody archer, and a glowing Fever thermometer, colorful cartoon biology style

storybook_pages.title: Healthy Body, Strong Mind
storybook_pages.text: Each pathogen wave teaches you about real immunology. By surviving all waves, you've learned how your body fights infections every day — from the common cold to serious diseases. Knowledge is your best vaccine!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: healthy body silhouette glowing with a protective shield, defeated pathogens scattered around, immune cells celebrating victory, DNA helix in the background, bright cheerful cartoon educational style

rounds.coaching_moment: Think carefully about the trade-offs before committing to this path.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you make this choice?

transfer_exercises.game_context: Prioritizing which threats to defend against first
transfer_exercises.real_world: Triaging tasks and problems by impact and urgency
transfer_exercises.challenge: Use the Eisenhower matrix to categorize your current tasks. Are you spending time on what actually matters?

transfer_exercises.real_world: Keeping quality high when workload unexpectedly doubles
transfer_exercises.challenge: Design a personal 'defense system' — habits and routines that protect your performance under stress.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: India carries a significant burden of both infectious and non-communicable diseases. Understanding how the immune system works — and how to support it — is part of India's health literacy agenda under NEP 2020.
reflection_prompt: Where did your defenses bend before they broke? What would you reinforce first next time?
